title: New York City Bans AI Tools in Schools for Younger Students
subtitle: The city’s new policy aims to protect human connection in the classroom while officials study the impact of technology on learning.

summary.en: New York City has announced a one-year ban on artificial intelligence tools for elementary and middle school students. The policy affects 600,000 students and stops the use of 40 different educational programs. Mayor Zohran Mamdani stated that children need human interaction and teachers to grow properly. While younger students are restricted, high schoolers will participate in pilot programs and literacy classes. Other school districts across the United States are watching this decision closely as they develop their own rules.
summary.zh: 紐約市宣布對小學和國中學生實施為期一年的人工智慧工具禁令。該政策影響六十萬名學生，並停止使用四十種不同的教育程式。市長曼達尼表示，兒童需要人際互動與教師引導才能健全成長。雖然年幼學生受到限制，但高中生將參與試點計畫與素養課程。美國其他學區在制定自身規範時，正密切關注此項決策。

paragraphs.en: New York City has introduced a significant change to its public school system. Starting this school year, elementary and middle school students will no longer be allowed to use generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools in the classroom. A moratorium — a temporary official stop to an activity — will last for one year. This decision affects approximately 600,000 students, making it the largest policy of its kind in the United States. According to Al Jazeera, the city will use this time to study how these tools affect children.
paragraphs.zh: 紐約市對其公立學校系統實施了一項重大變革。從本學年開始，小學和國中學生將不得在課堂上使用生成式人工智慧工具。這項為期一年的禁令，意指官方暫時停止某項活動。此項決策影響約六十萬名學生，是美國同類政策中規模最大的一項。根據半島電視台（Al Jazeera）報導，紐約市將利用這段時間研究這些工具對兒童的影響。

paragraphs.en: Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced the plan on Wednesday, emphasizing the importance of human relationships in education. He explained that children need to learn by working with their teachers and classmates, and by solving difficult problems on their own. "The tech industry wants us to believe that AI-powered early education is not only inevitable, but necessary. We do not see it that way," the mayor said during a news conference. Deutsche Welle reported that the city will stop the use of about 40 different educational AI tools that were previously used in classrooms.
paragraphs.zh: 市長曼達尼（Zohran Mamdani）於週三宣布這項計畫，強調人際關係在教育中的重要性。他解釋說，孩子們需要透過與老師和同學合作，以及自行解決難題來學習。市長在記者會上表示：「科技產業希望我們相信，由人工智慧驅動的早期教育不僅不可避免，而且是必要的。我們並不這麼認為。」德國之聲（Deutsche Welle）報導，紐約市將停止使用先前在課堂上使用的約四十種教育類人工智慧工具。

paragraphs.en: While the ban applies to younger students, it does not mean that all technology is leaving the classroom. Teachers will still be allowed to use AI to help with lesson planning and administrative tasks, such as scheduling. Additionally, high school students are exempt from the full ban. Instead, the city plans to launch pilot programs where a limited number of high schoolers can use specific AI platforms under the supervision of their teachers. These students will also receive AI literacy classes twice a year to help them understand how the technology works.
paragraphs.zh: 雖然這項禁令適用於年幼學生，但並不代表所有科技都將退出課堂。教師仍可使用人工智慧協助課程規劃與行政事務，例如排程。此外，高中生不受全面禁令限制。相反地，紐約市計畫啟動試點計畫，讓少數高中生能在教師監督下使用特定的人工智慧平台。這些學生每年還將接受兩次人工智慧素養課程，以幫助他們理解該技術的運作方式。

paragraphs.en: This new policy is part of a larger effort to manage screen time and improve student focus. The city is introducing new limits on how long students can use screens each day. Students in grades three through five will have a 30-minute daily cap, while students in grades six through eight will be limited to 45 minutes. Furthermore, the city has decided to ban "companion chatbots" — software programs designed to act like a friend or assistant — across all grade levels, including high schools.
paragraphs.zh: 這項新政策是管理螢幕使用時間並提升學生專注力之更大計畫的一部分。紐約市正在對學生每日使用螢幕的時間實施新限制。三至五年級學生的每日上限為三十分鐘，六至八年級學生則限制為四十五分鐘。此外，紐約市決定在所有年級（包括高中）禁止「陪伴型聊天機器人」，即那些設計用來扮演朋友或助理角色的軟體程式。

paragraphs.en: This decision comes at a difficult time for the city's schools. According to Al Jazeera, reading proficiency scores for students in grades three through eight dropped by 6 percent in 2025. By pausing the use of AI, the city hopes to create a space where educators and parents can better understand how these tools influence learning. Adin Lenchner, a political consultant based in New York, told Al Jazeera that many people were waiting for this kind of leadership, noting that the mayor is giving schools the "runway" to study the real impact of these tools on the education system.
paragraphs.zh: 這項決策是在紐約市學校面臨困難時期所做出的。根據半島電視台報導，三至八年級學生的閱讀能力分數在二〇二五年下降了百分之六。透過暫停使用人工智慧，紐約市希望創造一個空間，讓教育工作者與家長能更深入了解這些工具如何影響學習。駐紐約的政治顧問倫奇納（Adin Lenchner）告訴半島電視台，許多人都在等待這樣的領導力，並指出市長正在為學校提供「緩衝空間」，以研究這些工具對教育系統的實際影響。

paragraphs.en: New York is not the only city reconsidering its approach to technology. According to Deutsche Welle, the Los Angeles Unified school district, which is the second-largest in the country, is also blocking generative AI tools while it creates a formal policy. Like New York, Los Angeles has already set screen-time limits for younger students. While at least 37 states have some form of official guidance regarding AI, there is currently no consistent national standard for how schools should teach AI literacy.
paragraphs.zh: 紐約並非唯一重新評估科技應用方式的城市。根據德國之聲報導，全美第二大的洛杉磯聯合學區（Los Angeles Unified school district）也在制定正式政策的同時，封鎖了生成式人工智慧工具。與紐約一樣，洛杉磯已針對年幼學生設定了螢幕使用時間限制。儘管至少有三十七個州針對人工智慧制定了某種形式的官方指導方針，但目前對於學校應如何教授人工智慧素養，尚無一致的國家標準。

paragraphs.en: Reactions to the ban have been mixed. Some education advocates support the focus on human connection and the new screen-time limits. However, others have raised concerns about the details of the plan. Michael Mulgrew, president of the United Federation of Teachers, told the Associated Press that the policy leaves many questions unanswered. He specifically mentioned that the Department of Education needs to explain how it will ensure that the tools it does purchase are safe and effective for students.
paragraphs.zh: 各界對此禁令反應不一。部分教育倡議者支持將重點放在人際連結與新的螢幕使用時間限制上。然而，其他人則對計畫細節提出疑慮。美國教師聯合會（United Federation of Teachers）主席穆格魯（Michael Mulgrew）告訴美聯社（Associated Press），該政策留下許多未解的問題。他特別提到，教育局需要說明將如何確保所採購的工具對學生而言是安全且有效的。

paragraphs.en: As other school districts across the country watch New York, experts believe this move could set a standard for how American schools handle the rise of AI. Margeret Murry. The city plans to use the next year to evaluate the results of its pilot programs and the general impact of the ban. For now, the focus remains on ensuring that technology serves as a helpful tool rather than a replacement for the essential relationship between students and their teachers.
paragraphs.zh: 隨著全國其他學區密切關注紐約，專家認為此舉可能為美國學校處理人工智慧興起的方式樹立標準。紐約市計畫利用接下來的一年評估試點計畫的結果以及禁令的整體影響。目前，重點仍放在確保科技作為有用的工具，而非取代學生與教師之間不可或缺的關係。

keyTerms.definitionEn: A limit on the amount of something that is allowed.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（帽子），這裡指數量上的限制。文中：Students in grades three through five will have a 30-minute daily cap, while students in grades six through eight will be limited to 45 minutes.

keyTerms.definitionEn: A period of time or space allowed for a project to develop or be tested.
keyTerms.definitionZh: （給予計畫發展或測試的）時間、空間或緩衝期。
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（飛機跑道），這裡比喻給予學校進行研究的緩衝時間。文中：Adin Lenchner, a political consultant based in New York, told Al Jazeera that many people were waiting for this kind of leadership, noting that the mayor is giving schools the "runway" to study the real impact of these tools on the education system.

keyTerms.definitionEn: Consisting of different, often opposing, opinions or feelings.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 褒貶不一的、意見分歧的。
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作動詞（混合）的過去分詞，這裡形容反應不一致。文中：Reactions to the ban have been mixed.

quiz.question: Which of the following is true regarding the new technology policies in New York City public schools?

options.A: High school students are completely prohibited from using any AI tools.
options.B: Teachers are still permitted to use AI for administrative purposes like scheduling.
options.C: The ban on generative AI tools will be a permanent change to the school system.
options.D: All students, regardless of grade, are now restricted to 30 minutes of screen time daily.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第三段，教師仍被允許使用 AI 來協助課程規劃與行政事務（如排程）。選項 A 錯誤，因為高中生被豁免於全面禁令，且有試辦計畫；選項 C 錯誤，文中明確指出這是一個為期一年的暫時性禁令（moratorium）；選項 D 錯誤，因為 30 分鐘的限制僅針對三至五年級學生，六至八年級則是 45 分鐘。

quiz.question: What can be inferred about the city's motivation for implementing these new policies?

options.A: The city believes AI tools are inherently harmful and should never be used in education.
options.B: The city is trying to save money by reducing the number of educational software subscriptions.
options.C: The city is prioritizing traditional learning methods while it gathers data on AI's long-term effects.
options.D: The city intends to replace all human teachers with more efficient AI-powered systems in the future.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據文章第一段與第五段，城市實施禁令是為了利用這一年時間研究 AI 對學習的影響，並強調人際關係的重要性。選項 A 太過極端，因為高中生仍有試辦計畫；選項 B 文章未提及節省開支；選項 D 與市長強調「人際關係」的立場完全相反，故不正確。

quiz.question: In the fifth paragraph, what does the author mean by the phrase 'giving schools the runway'?

options.A: Providing schools with the necessary time and space to prepare or test something.
options.B: Building physical infrastructure for new technology programs in classrooms.
options.C: Allowing schools to quickly abandon old teaching methods for new ones.
options.D: Giving schools more financial resources to hire additional staff.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。在此上下文中，「runway」（跑道）是一個比喻用法，意指給予學校足夠的空間、時間或條件來進行測試或準備，以便觀察 AI 的真實影響。選項 B、C、D 皆與此比喻的意涵不符，且文中並未提及提供額外資金或建設硬體設施。

quiz.question: What is the primary message of this article?

options.A: New York City has successfully eliminated all digital distractions from its classrooms.
options.B: AI technology is rapidly becoming the most important tool for modern American students.
options.C: New York City is pausing AI use in schools to evaluate its impact while prioritizing human-led instruction.
options.D: Teachers are protesting the new AI ban because they feel it prevents them from doing their jobs.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。全文的核心在於報導紐約市針對中小學實施 AI 禁令，目的是為了在科技與傳統教學之間取得平衡，並利用這段時間進行評估。選項 A 太過絕對；選項 B 與文章強調限制 AI 的立場相左；選項 D 雖然提到工會領袖對政策細節有疑慮，但並非全文的主旨。
